result.topic_en: Continuation of a geometric proof relating to Ribaucour's propositions: it derives a formula for the ratio of radii of curvature at corresponding points M and M′ and states that, for a conic, the ratio of the radii of curvature at two points equals the cube of the ratio of the tangent lengths from their intersection.

male en K à (K) avec NM, NM'. Posons
$\widehat{NM}\,M' = \hat{\theta}, \qquad \widehat{NM'}\,M = \theta', \qquad \widehat{MK}\,\alpha = \hat{\varphi}, \qquad M'\widehat{K\beta} = \varphi',$
nous aurons
$\frac{d(M)}{d(M')} = \frac{MK}{M'K}\,\frac{TM}{TM'}, \qquad d(K) = K\alpha\,\frac{d(M)}{M\mu} = K\beta\,\frac{d(M')}{M'\mu'},$
d'où
$\frac{KM}{KM'}\,\frac{TM}{TM'} = \frac{M\mu}{M'\mu'}\,\frac{KM'}{KM}\,\frac{\cos\varphi}{\cos\varphi'}, \qquad \frac{\overline{MK}^2}{\overline{M'K}^2}\,\frac{TM}{TM'} = \frac{M\mu}{M'\mu'}\,\frac{\cos\varphi}{\cos\varphi'},$
d'où, en remarquant que $\frac{MS}{\cos\varphi} = \frac{KS}{\cos\theta}$, $\frac{M'S}{\cos\varphi'} = \frac{KS}{\cos\theta'}$,
$\frac{MS}{M'S} : \frac{MT}{M'T} = \frac{M'\mu'}{M\mu}\,\frac{\cos^3\theta'}{\cos^3\theta},$
d'où enfin
$\frac{\rho M'}{\rho M} = \frac{MS}{M'S}\,\frac{M'T}{MT}\,\frac{\overline{KM'}^3}{\overline{KM}^3}.$
Un cas particulièrement simple sera celui où le rap-
port $\frac{MS}{M'S} : \frac{MT}{M'T}$ sera harmonique; nous aurons alors
$\frac{\rho_{M'}}{\rho_{M}} = \frac{\overline{KM'}^3}{\overline{KM}^3}.$
En voici deux exemples géométriques :
1° Les courbes (M) et (M') sont une seule et même
conique, la courbe (K) est une droite. On voit que :
Si les deux tangentes à une conique en M et M' se
coupent en K, le rapport des rayons de courbure à
cette courbe en M et M' est égal au cube du rap-
port $\frac{KM}{KM'}$.
result.notes_en: The page contains no question statements. It continues the argument of the article on Ribaucour's two propositions (Questions 858, 859). Angles θ, θ′, φ, φ′ are defined. Differential relations between the arcs d(M), d(M′) and d(K) then lead to the result that ρM′/ρM equals (MS/M′S)(M′T/MT)(KM′³/KM³). When the ratio (MS/M′S):(MT/M′T) is harmonic, this reduces to ρM′/ρM = KM′³/KM³. The first of two geometric examples follows: when (M) and (M′) are the same conic and (K) is a line, the ratio of the radii of curvature at M and M′ equals the cube of KM/KM′, where K is the intersection of the tangents at M and M′.
